claim: 70-kDa Heat shock proteins are ATP-driven molecular chaperones that perform a myriad of essential cellular tasks.
source: 70-kDa Heat shock proteins are ATP-driven molecular chaperones that perform a myriad of essential cellular tasks.
evidence: This is a general statement about Hsp70 proteins supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Energy consumption due to ATP-hydrolysis can decrease the dissociation constant of the chaperone-substrate complex by several orders of magnitude with respect to an equilibrium scenario.
source: Energy consumption can indeed decrease the dissociation constant of the chaperone-substrate complex by several orders of magnitude with respect to an equilibrium scenario.
evidence: This claim is supported by the theoretical model and calculations presented in the manuscript, particularly shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The biochemical requirements for observing ultra-affinity coincide with the physiological conditions in the cell.
source: We find that the biochemical requirements for observing such ultra-affinity coincide with the physiological conditions in the cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of the model parameters and their comparison with known cellular conditions.

claim: Hsp70s are possibly the most ubiquitous molecular chaperones.
source: 70-kDa Heat shock proteins (Hsp70s) stand out for several reasons: they are possibly the most ubiquitous
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about the distribution of Hsp70 proteins.

claim: Hsp70s function as monomers.
source: they function as monomers
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsp70 structure and function.

claim: Hsp70s supervise protein translation.
source: they supervise a plethora of diverse cellular processes (Mayer and Bukau, 2005; Zuiderweg et al., 2013) such as protein translation (Kramer et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kramer et al., 2009.

claim: Hsp70s supervise protein trafficking.
source: protein trafficking (Matlack et al., 1999; Neupert and Brunner, 2002)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Matlack et al., 1999 and Neupert and Brunner, 2002.

claim: Hsp70s supervise the disassembly of protein complexes.
source: the disassembly of protein complexes (Böcking et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Böcking et al., 2011.

claim: Hsp70s supervise signaling.
source: signaling (Pratt and Toft, 2003)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pratt and Toft, 2003.

claim: Hsp70s supervise protein degradation.
source: protein degradation (Hohfeld et al., 2001)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hohfeld et al., 2001.

claim: All Hsp70 cellular tasks crucially depend on the high-affinity binding of Hsp70s to substrate proteins during a complex ATP-driven conformational cycle.
source: All these tasks crucially depend on the high-affinity binding of Hsp70s to substrate proteins during a complex ATP-driven conformational cycle (Mayer, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mayer, 2013.

claim: The ATP- and ADP-bound states of Hsp70 and their interconversion play a major role in the chaperone functional cycle.
source: The ATP- and ADP-bound states of Hsp70 (Hsp70⋅ATP and Hsp70⋅ADP respectively) and their interconversion play a major role in the chaperone functional cycle
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsp70 function.

claim: The nature of the bound nucleotide affects the affinity of the chaperone for its substrates.
source: the nature of the bound nucleotide affects the affinity of the chaperone for its substrates, with Hsp70⋅ADP binding the substrate more stably than Hsp70⋅ATP (Schmid et al., 1994; Theyssen et al., 1996; Packschies et al., 1997; Gisler et al., 1998; Russell et al., 1998; Laufen et al., 1999; Mayer et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Hsp70⋅ADP binds the substrate more stably than Hsp70⋅ATP.
source: with Hsp70⋅ADP binding the substrate more stably than Hsp70⋅ATP (Schmid et al., 1994; Theyssen et al., 1996; Packschies et al., 1997; Gisler et al., 1998; Russell et al., 1998; Laufen et al., 1999; Mayer et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The effective affinity of Hsp70 for substrates when the chaperone was running through its ATP-hydrolysis driven cycle was significantly higher than both the ones of Hsp70⋅ATP and Hsp70⋅ADP.
source: several experimental evidences suggested that the effective affinity of Hsp70 for substrates when the chaperone was running through its ATP-hydrolysis driven cycle was significantly higher than both the ones of Hsp70⋅ATP and Hsp70⋅ADP (Laufen et al., 1999; Wittung-Stafshede et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The remarkable result of higher effective affinity during the ATP-hydrolysis cycle would not be possible within the boundaries of thermodynamic equilibrium.
source: Because this remarkable result would not be possible within the boundaries of thermodynamic equilibrium, it is therefore necessary to clarify how ATP hydrolysis, and thus energy consumption, can affect the binding strength of Hsp70s to their substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from thermodynamic principles.

claim: Substrate binding/unbinding takes place with rates that depend on the state of the bound nucleotide.
source: According to the consensus Hsp70 cycle (Figure 1) substrate binding/unbinding takes place with rates that depend on the state of the bound nucleotide (kATPon, kATPoff, kADPon, kADPoff) (Schmid et al., 1994; Gisler et al., 1998; Mayer et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Hsp70⋅ATP exchanges the substrate two to three orders of magnitude faster than Hsp70⋅ADP.
source: with Hsp70⋅ATP exchanging the substrate two to three orders of magnitude faster than Hsp70⋅ADP.
evidence: This is based on established kinetic measurements in the literature.

claim: J-domain proteins enhance the rate of ATP hydrolysis.
source: J-domain proteins (JDPs) enhance the rate of ATP hydrolysis
evidence: This is supported by citation to Youker and Brodsky, 2007 and Kampinga and Craig, 2010.

claim: Nucleotide exchange factors catalyze nucleotide release.
source: nucleotide exchange factors (NEFs) catalyze nucleotide release (Youker and Brodsky, 2007; Kampinga and Craig, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: JDPs bind the substrate and subsequently interact with Hsp70, enhancing ATP hydrolysis.
source: In particular, JDPs are known to bind the substrate and subsequently interact with Hsp70, enhancing ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about JDP mechanism.

claim: ATP-hydrolysis results into a net production of ADP and a loss of ATP.
source: ATP-hydrolysis, at variance with exchange, results into a net production of ADP and a loss of ATP.
evidence: This is basic biochemical knowledge about ATP hydrolysis.

claim: In a cellular perspective, the ATP and ADP concentrations are kept fixed by energy-consuming chemostats.
source: In a cellular perspective, the ATP and ADP concentrations are kept fixed by energy-consuming chemostats.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cellular energy metabolism.

claim: In vivo, ATP hydrolysis is an intrinsically non-equilibrium process.
source: In vivo, ATP hydrolysis is therefore an intrinsically non-equilibrium process.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that ATP/ADP concentrations are maintained by chemostats.

claim: In the absence of hydrolysis, no energy is consumed and all the reactions of the Hsp70 cycle are at equilibrium.
source: In the absence of hydrolysis, no energy is consumed and all the reactions of the Hsp70 cycle are at equilibrium.
evidence: This is based on thermodynamic principles.

claim: At equilibrium, the detailed balance rule holds and each branch of the biochemical cycle is individually balanced.
source: In this scenario, where all the reactions are driven by thermal fluctuations, the detailed balance rule holds and each branch of the biochemical cycle is individually balanced ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a fundamental principle of equilibrium thermodynamics.

claim: The equilibrium dissociation constant can be measured in experiments where Hsp70 hydrolysis deficient mutants are used.
source: The equilibrium dissociation constant can be in principle measured in experiments where Hsp70 hydrolysis deficient mutants are used (McCarty and Walker, 1991), at varying ratios of the concentrations of the two nucleotides.
evidence: This is supported by citation to McCarty and Walker, 1991.

claim: When ATP hydrolysis is turned on, the dissipated energy must be taken into account in the energy budget along the cycle.
source: At variance with equilibrium, when ATP hydrolysis is turned on, the energy budget along the cycle is not restricted to the free-energy differences between the different states. Rather, the dissipated energy Ediss, which is related to ATP hydrolysis, must be taken into account.
evidence: This is based on non-equilibrium thermodynamics principles.

claim: When ATP hydrolysis is turned on, detailed balance is broken.
source: Thus detailed balance is broken and pairwise reactions cannot be solved individually as in the equilibrium case.
evidence: This is a consequence of non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

claim: Even in non-equilibrium conditions a steady-state solution of the cycle exists.
source: Nonetheless, even in non-equilibrium conditions a steady-state solution of the cycle exists ('Materials and methods')
evidence: This is demonstrated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The hydrolysis flux increases with k_h^S/k_h before saturation.
source: Not surprisingly, the hydrolysis flux increases with khS/kh, before saturation, corresponding to a regime dominated by the rate-limiting exchange process (Gassler et al., 2001).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and supported by citation.

claim: Non-equilibrium conditions lead to a dramatic increase of the affinity of Hsp70s for their substrates that could not be achieved at equilibrium.
source: Non-equilibrium conditions lead thus to a dramatic increase of the affinity of Hsp70s for their substrates, that could not be achieved at equilibrium, where the effective dissociation constant would be bounded between the ones of the ATP-bound and ADP-bound states.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the model results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The theoretical lower bound regime corresponds to substrate binding exclusively to Hsp70⋅ATP and being released exclusively from the ADP-bound state.
source: This regime corresponds to the limiting case of substrate binding exclusively to Hsp70⋅ATP, which has the fastest binding rate, and being released exclusively from the ADP-bound state, which has the slowest unbinding rate.
evidence: This is inferred from the mathematical analysis of the limiting case.

claim: The theoretical limit of ultra-affinity likely pertains to a regime that is not accessible to Hsp70s.
source: Our analysis indicates that this theoretical limit, recently hinted at (Zuiderweg et al., 2013), likely pertains to a regime that is not accessible to Hsp70s.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis and supported by citation.

claim: The lower bound of K_eff^neq depends on the kinetic properties of the cycle and does not rely on the dissociation constants of any nucleotide-bound state.
source: It must be stressed here that this lower bound, as well as ultra-affinity, depends on the kinetic properties of the cycle and does not rely on the dissociation constants of any nucleotide-bound state.
evidence: This is inferred from the mathematical analysis.

claim: Ultra-affinity can be achieved only for k_ADP^off/k_ATP^off < 1.
source: For kADPoff≥kATPoff the non-equilibrium dissociation constant is bound to the equilibrium range. Ultra-affinity can be achieved only for kADPoff/kATPoff<1
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ultra-affinity is more pronounced for larger time-scale separations.
source: and is more pronounced for larger time-scale separations.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: At equilibrium, dissociation constants do not depend on the total species concentration.
source: Indeed, at equilibrium, dissociation constants do not depend on the total species concentration since they simply encode the difference of free-energy between the bound and unbound states.
evidence: This is based on equilibrium thermodynamics principles.

claim: There is a sharp transition in K_eff^neq behavior at [S]tot/[Hsp70]tot = 1.
source: Two distinct regimes can be observed here with a sharp transition occuring at [S]tot/[Hsp70]tot = 1.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the excess of chaperone ([S]tot/[Hsp70]tot<1), ultra-affinity is observed.
source: In the excess of chaperone ([S]tot/[Hsp70]tot<1) we observe ultra-affinity and the previously described behavior
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In substrate excess conditions, substrate binding to ADP-bound state becomes dominant and the system cannot exploit the time-scale separation in binding/unbinding kinetics to achieve ultra-affinity.
source: This effect can be easily rationalized considering that in the latter condition, substrate binding to ADP-bound state becomes dominant and the system cannot exploit the time-scale separation in binding/unbinding kinetics to achieve ultra-affinity.
evidence: This is inferred from the model analysis.

claim: The experimental characterization of the Hsp70-substrate dissociation constant in physiological, non-equilibrium conditions is extremely limited.
source: Quite surprisingly, the experimental characterization of the Hsp70-substrate dissociation constant in physiological, non-equilibrium conditions is extremely limited.
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the literature.

claim: Ultra-affinity was implicitly suggested in works assessing the binding of different substrates to Hsp70s in the presence of a co-localized JDP.
source: However, ultra-affinity was implicitely suggested in a series of works assessing the binding of different substrates to Hsp70s, always in the presence of a co-localized JDP, thus ensuring maximal hydrolysis acceleration upon substrate binding (Misselwitz et al., 1998; Laufen et al., 1999; Sullivan et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: In assays with co-localized JDP, the substrate was observed to bind more efficiently in the presence of ATP than in the presence of ADP.
source: In all these assays the substrate was observed to bind more efficiently in the presence of ATP, that drives the chaperone through its cycle, than in the presence of ADP, that instead blocks the system in the Hsp70⋅ADP state, the one with the lowest thermodynamic dissociation constant.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations cited in the manuscript.

claim: Ultra-affinity becomes manifest when substrate binding is coupled with enhanced hydrolysis acceleration by the colocalization of the Hsp70 binding region and of a J-domain.
source: All these findings strongly suggest that ultra-affinity becomes manifest when substrate binding is coupled with enhanced hydrolysis acceleration by the colocalization of the Hsp70 binding region and of a J-domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations and model predictions.

claim: The substrate-exchange rates of the ADP-bound state must be significantly slower than the ATP-state for Hsp70 to exhibit ultra-affinity.
source: Our analysis of the cycle has unveiled the conditions that Hsp70 must satisfy to exhibit ultra-affinity: (i) the substrate-exchange rates of the ADP-bound state must be significantly slower than the ATP-state so that extremely different timescales can be exploited
evidence: This is inferred from the model analysis.

claim: ATP hydrolysis must be enhanced by orders of magnitude to fully enter the ultra-affinity regime.
source: (ii) ATP hydrolysis must be enhanced by orders of magnitude to fully enter the ultra-affinity regime
evidence: This is inferred from the model analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The chaperone must be in excess over the substrate for ultra-affinity.
source: (iii) the chaperone must be in excess over the substrate.
evidence: This is inferred from the model analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All conditions for ultra-affinity are typically met in the cell by canonical Hsp70 chaperones.
source: All these conditions are typically met in the cell by canonical Hsp70 chaperones, such as bacterial DnaK and cytosolic Hsc70 in eukaryotes
evidence: This is based on knowledge of cellular conditions and Hsp70 properties.

claim: Hsp70⋅ADP has limited exchange kinetics.
source: Hsp70⋅ADP is known to have limited exchange kinetics
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsp70.

claim: Hsp70s work only in partnership with JDPs.
source: Hsp70s are known to work only in partnership with JDPs
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsp70 function.

claim: Hsp70s are highly abundant and typically in excess over JDPs.
source: Hsp70s are highly abundant and typically in excess over JDPs (Finka and Goloubinoff, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Cellular conditions are optimal for ultra-affinity.
source: Cellular conditions seem thus to be optimal for ultra-affinity.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of cellular conditions and model requirements.

claim: ATP hydrolysis can be exploited by cells to overcome the constraints set by equilibrium thermodynamics.
source: Our results provide an additional example of how ATP hydrolysis can be exploited by cells to overcome the constraints set by equilibrium thermodynamics.
evidence: This is inferred from the results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The key role of energy consumption in driving biochemical cycles for performing a variety of functions is well established.
source: The key role of energy consumption in driving biochemical cycles for performing a variety of functions is well established (Schnakenberg 1976; Hill, 2005; Ge et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Energy consumption has been recognized in cellular processes such as sensing, signaling and adaptation.
source: and recently it has been recognized in cellular processes such as sensing, signaling and adaptation (Qian and Reluga, 2005; Lan et al., 2012; Mehta and Schwab, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Ultra-affinity shares similarities with kinetic proofreading in that both use chemical energy consumption to increase binding affinity beyond equilibrium values.
source: Notably, the ultra-affinity concept proposed here shares some similarities with the well-known kinetic proofreading (Hopfield, 1974) since in both cases chemical energy consumption is used to increase the binding affinity of specific molecules beyond their equilibrium value.
evidence: This is a comparison based on conceptual analysis and supported by citation.

claim: Kinetic proofreading exploits multiple non-equilibrium steps to enhance a pre-existing difference in binding affinity among various substrates.
source: kinetic proofreading exploits multiple non-equilibrium steps to enhance a pre-existing difference in binding affinity among various substrates
evidence: This is established knowledge about kinetic proofreading.

claim: Ultra-affinity is achieved due to the specific ability of the substrate to induce upon binding a non-equilibrium transition in the receptor.
source: whereas ultra-affinity is achieved due to the specific ability of the substrate to induce upon binding a non-equilibrium transition in the receptor (i.e., the chaperone).
evidence: This is inferred from the mechanism described in the manuscript.

claim: A similar approach may be applicable to more specialized Hsp70s, such as HscA.
source: We expect that a similar approach may be applicable to more specialized Hsp70s, such as HscA (Hesterkamp and Bukau, 1998)
evidence: This is speculation supported by citation.

claim: A similar approach may be applicable to other chaperones with more complex cycles, such as the GroEL/S system, Hsp100s and Hsp90s.
source: and to other chaperones, with possibly more complex cycles, such as the GroEL/S system, Hsp100s and Hsp90s.
evidence: This is speculation about potential applications.

claim: Other molecular machines might work along the same principles as ultra-affinity.
source: As well, it would not be surprising to discover other molecular machines working along the same principles, so that the present study might also provide a general scheme applicable beyond Hsp70 chaperones.
evidence: This is speculation about broader applicability.

claim: The deterministic mass-balance equation treatment is appropriate for the Hsp70 system since both chaperones and substrates are highly abundant in standard cellular conditions.
source: We frame here the model in terms of deterministic mass-balance equations, which describe the evolution of the concentrations of the different states. This treatment is appropriate for the Hsp70 system since both chaperones and substrates are highly abundant in standard cellular conditions.
evidence: This is a methodological justification based on knowledge of cellular conditions.

claim: In the case of less abundant molecular species, fluctuations might not be negligible and a stochastic description would be required.
source: In the case of less abundant molecular species fluctuations might not be negligible. Therefore a more detailed, stochastic description of the process would be required (Ge et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on theoretical considerations and supported by citation.

claim: Nucleotide release rates are much slower than nucleotide binding rates.
source: Typically the nucleotide release rates are much slower than the nucleotide binding rates (Table 1)
evidence: This is based on the experimental parameters listed in Table 1.

claim: The dimerization of DnaJ into DnaJ2 has been considered as implicit in the model.
source: The dimerization of DnaJ into DnaJ2 has also been considered as implicit.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the model.

claim: The rate of synthesis of ATP from ADP is neglected because it was experimentally proven to be below the level of detectability.
source: The rate of synthesis of ATP from ADP (the microscopic reverse of hydrolysis) is neglected here because it was experimentally proven to be below the level of detectability even in the presence of the hydrolysis-accelerating JDP cochaperones (Russell et al., 1998), that is ksynth≤10−6 s−1.
evidence: This is justified by citation to experimental data.

claim: The ratio [ATP]/[ADP] = 10 approximately matches the physiological ratio.
source: The ratio [ATP]/[ADP] = 10 has been used throughout the calculations, approximately matching the physiological ratio.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of cellular nucleotide concentrations.
